sections.heading: Sharing model
sections.markdown:
The following are settled target contracts; complete go, Task, resource, and synchronization families require separate implementation qualification under spec §17.

- `const` fixes a binding and its value-semantic components, without freezing class objects or proving Sendable
- go arguments and captures must be Sendable, checked over the complete type; COW or atomic reference counts alone are insufficient
- a go closure may not capture any ordinary outer `var`, even for reads; pass copyable, Sendable local values explicitly and retain the caller's logical copy
- const values and copyable non-view READ values may be captured by value when Sendable; qualified synchronization handles retain their synchronized identity
- Array copying does not require `copy(array)` or unique backing; copying stops at class and synchronization identities
- ref and Slice/MutSlice loans cannot enter go; noncopyable Sendable resources transfer only through declared consuming parameters
- shared mutation requires qualified channels or synchronization objects; const, a short scope, or unsafe cannot waive the boundary requirements

sections.heading: await all
sections.markdown: Waiting uses `await task`, without an `await (move task)` form. The target Task result domain is copyable and Sendable; backing uniqueness does not select result ownership. `await all` uses a homogeneous collection of `Task<T>` values and produces `Array<T>`. Complete waiting, repeated observation, failure, and cancellation behavior must be frozen and qualified with the Task declaration family; this card does not claim that family is implemented.

sections.heading: Value arguments
sections.markdown: Passing a copyable, Sendable Array as an explicit go argument preserves the caller's logical copy. Noncopyable resources use the callee's consuming declaration; an explicit move marker does not make a non-Sendable value transferable. These target rules do not admit the complete go declaration family.

sections.heading: Atomic
sections.markdown:
`Atomic<T>` wraps `i64`/`f64`/`bool` with lock-free atomic operations. Name it with `const`; its audited methods provide synchronized interior mutation. Methods: `load`, `store`, `add`, `sub`, `fetchAdd`, `fetchSub`, `swap`, `compareExchange`, `toggle`. Optional `Ordering` enum parameter (default `SeqCst`).

Frozen next cutover: Ordering uses an owned governed nominal identity, with ordinary visibility/construction/dependency checks. compareExchange prepares a real owned Tuple before any cell access. Each f64 RMW resume attempts at most one cell CAS and continues in the same frame after failure. Complete Atomic execution remains pending implementation and qualification (spec 10.9).

sections.heading: Synchronization handles
sections.markdown: Name `Channel`, `Atomic`, coroutine-domain `sync.*` handles, and OS-thread-domain `sys.Os*` handles with `const`. Use `sync.*` inside coroutine code; use `sys.Os*` inside `sys.Thread` or other blocking OS-thread contexts.
